name: Omnia
subtitle: Your own add-ons, on every Apple device.
description: Omnia plays what your own Stremio add-ons, playlists and media servers provide. It hosts no content.

apps.name: Omnia
apps.subtitle: Your own add-ons, on every Apple device.
apps.localizedDescription: Omnia is a media player for your own Stremio add-ons, Live TV playlists, and Jellyfin or Emby servers. It hosts no content: everything you watch comes from sources you add yourself.

versions.localizedDescription:
KSPlayer sound and subtitles fixed, and a rebuilt Settings.

Fixed
- KSPlayer (experimental): sound plays and you can switch audio tracks, and subtitles stay on screen until each line ends.
- The Mac build no longer fails on KSPlayer's FFmpeg placeholder frameworks, and Omnia's own code builds without warnings.

New
- Settings is one list on every device, with no Advanced pages: every option is on its page, under clear headings. The playback Engine, mpv or KSPlayer, is first on Settings › Player.
- Hero Catalogs, Add-ons and Plugins fold open into lists you can reorder by dragging or with each row's menu. Plugin order is kept when a repository refreshes.
- Clearer controls: system switches, pop-up menus with a checkmark, and text fields that outline themselves while you type.
- On Mac, Settings rows highlight edge to edge when you hover or click, as on iPhone.

Fixes for the player, Continue Watching and the KSPlayer engine.

Fixed
- Skip Intro, Recap, Outro and Credits and Up Next keep the player controls hidden until you use them or they end. Up Next's Cancel also puts the card away.
- Titles in Continue Watching from Trakt or Simkl resume where you left off instead of starting over.
- KSPlayer (experimental): sound plays, and embedded subtitles that appear after the video starts are listed and picked.
- KSPlayer's Picture in Picture opens on the live picture, without a black start.
- mpv's Picture in Picture on iPhone and iPad is back to how it was in 0.4.0.

A second playback engine to try, smoother Picture in Picture, and a round of fixes.

New
- KSPlayer engine (experimental): Settings › Player › Advanced › Engine. mpv stays the default. KSPlayer uses the same controls, and on iPhone and iPad it floats every format, MKV included, smoothly in Picture in Picture, also when you swipe home. Dolby Vision dynamic metadata and styled .ass subtitles aren't supported in it yet, and Blu-ray discs on the Mac stay with mpv.
- Smooth Picture in Picture for MP4 and HLS streams with mpv: tapping the button hands the video to Apple's player at the same spot and audio track.
- The All, Movies and Series switch in Library is interactive glass you can drag across.
- MDBList's score can be turned off in its settings.

Improved
- Mac shows page titles in the toolbar, and the sidebar says Settings.
- iPad portrait fits better, including Settings search.
- The home hero shows up to 15 titles, without dots.
- Mark as Watched is gone from the home and title page heroes, and their buttons line up.
- Pulling down Control Center or Notification Center no longer pauses the video.

A big redesign: a cleaner player, a new Library and Continue Watching, and Settings that look the same on every device.

New
- Continue Watching cards in two styles, Card and Poster, with a menu from the ⋯ button, a long press or a right-click: Go to Show, Mark as Watched, Remove from Watchlist.
- Landscape Card Style: one place to size every landscape card, including Continue Watching and collections.
- A new Library: only the titles you've added, each once, with All, Movies and Series in a Liquid Glass switch.
- An Apple TV-style player: glass controls, a thin timeline you can tap or drag to seek, AirPlay, and pinch to fill or fit on iPhone and iPad.
- Mono accent, which adapts to light and dark, and system text and icon colours throughout.

Improved
- Settings are regrouped, with everyday options first and the rest on Advanced pages. Mac Settings now match iPhone and iPad.
- Native animations: the poster zooms into its title page, buttons respond with symbol effects, and iPhone gives haptic feedback.
- iPad shows sources on the full page, as on Mac.
- Cleanup, security checks and better power use: Omnia eases off when the device runs hot.

Removed
- Upcoming. New Episode Reminders still work.

Update all your devices together. Settings saved by 0.4.0 may not load on 0.3.9.

A new Settings on Mac and iPad with a live preview, and a sidebar you can hide.

New
- Settings on Mac and iPad now has a sidebar, with a live preview pinned at the top of each page. It follows the section you're editing.
- A sidebar button shows or hides the categories, so the page and preview can take the full width. Omnia remembers your choice. On Mac, the shortcut is Cmd+Ctrl+S.

Improved
- iPhone Settings is reorganised into Look, Watch, Sources and You, and its icons now match the style of the Mac and iPad sidebar.
- The Display section in Settings > Layout is split into Theme, Display, Hero Gradient and Top Bar.

Smoother Picture in Picture and trailers, less work while scrolling, and clearer settings.

Improved
- Tapping a hero trailer now carries on straight away in the player, with no restart, loading screen or slide.
- Picture in Picture comes back to the player without a loading screen, and keeps up with the sound better.
- Scrolling does less work on iPhone and iPad: cards no longer each carry their own page link. On Mac, a hero scrolled off screen no longer redraws the window.
- Hero fades use less graphics work over a playing trailer.
- On iPad and Mac, a playing trailer now ends in a short fade rather than a hard edge.

Fixed
- Gradient Overlay, with its strength and height sliders, is now under Dynamic Background Color in Settings > Layout.
- Top bar and player size sliders no longer show their names twice, and now show their values.
- The page's colour no longer flashes when a trailer starts or the hero changes.

Picture in Picture for every video on iPhone and iPad, Low Power Mode, App Lock, and more ways to size and style Omnia.

New
- Picture in Picture for videos played by Omnia's own player on iPhone and iPad, including MKV, from the button or when you swipe home. This is new and still needs testing on real devices, so tell us if the floating window stays black.
- While a video floats, you can keep using Omnia underneath. Coming back returns it to the player.
- Low Power Mode: turns off hero trailers and Omnia's glass. It follows your device's setting by default, or you can turn it on or off in Settings > Layout.
- New Episode Reminders: a notification on the day a new episode of a saved or in-progress series airs. Turn it on in Settings > Layout > Upcoming.
- App Lock: Face ID, Touch ID or your passcode for Settings and for switching profiles. Turn it on in Settings > Account.
- Player Appearance, in Settings > Playback: sliders for the size of player controls, timeline and menus with a live preview, together with all subtitle settings.
- Top Bar Size, Height and Width sliders on iPad and Mac.
- Gradient Overlay switch with strength and height sliders in Settings > Layout > Home Layout.

Improved
- Top bar tabs now respond the moment you touch them.
- Liquid Glass sliders are smooth, with the preview following your finger.
- The top bar's glass now matches the other controls.
- iPhone can now turn off the navigation bar's glass.
- A longer volume slider in the iPhone player.
- All artwork placeholders are now plain grey.
- On iPhone, the trailer mute button on title pages is now at the top right, as on Home.

Fixed
- Turning off Menus and Panels now removes glass from the source picker and other sheets.
- Sound should now play with your iPhone or iPad on silent, in the player and in trailers.
- Closing the floating video now stops playback.

Liquid Glass you can control, a smoother hero, and many fixes across iPhone, iPad and Mac.

New
- Liquid Glass settings, in Settings > Layout > Liquid Glass: an overall switch, a style, an intensity slider, separate switches for each part of the app, and a live preview.
- Show or hide the labels under Wide and Poster Continue Watching cards.
- Up to 6 hero catalogs instead of 2.

Improved
- Play, View Details and the other hero buttons now use Liquid Glass on iPhone and iPad, like the Mac.
- The hero now melts into the section below it, on Home and on title pages.
- A soft fade at the top of the hero covers the black bars some trailers have.
- On iPad and Mac, a playing trailer is no longer covered by the colour overlay.
- Hero dots are plain dots, with no pill behind them.
- Discover now has a magnifying glass icon.
- On iPhone, the trailer mute button moved to the top right, and the Profile tab glows in your accent colour.
- Player menus on iPhone are smaller and stay the same size in every aspect ratio.
- Player controls and menus now animate in and out, and follow Reduce Motion.
- Onboarding shows the real Home and title pages at the right scale on iPhone.

Fixed
- Top bar on iPad and Mac: tabs now respond across their whole area, not only on the icon and label.
- Opening a hero trailer in the player now continues where it was, instead of starting over.
- Onboarding: no oversized scrollbar, and the page dots no longer sit on the buttons or text.
- Updating from SideStore no longer sends you back through onboarding if you are signed in.
- The Picture in Picture button on iPhone and iPad now tells you when a video can't use it. MKV files and sources that need special headers can't float yet.

Collections are easier to organise, card styles now work per device, the iPad got a proper layout, and signing out on one device no longer signs you out everywhere.

New
- Drag to reorder collections. Each collection is one tidy row with a drag handle and show, edit and remove buttons.
- Apply to All Cards. One button on the Poster Card Style page copies its look to Collections, their folders and Continue Watching. It replaces the confusing "Match Poster Card Style" options.
- Card styles per device. A size that suits a Mac no longer changes your iPhone. Turn on Same Style on All Devices if you'd rather share one set.
- Cards in Folders setting. Choose how titles look inside a collection folder.
- Home background blend. With Dynamic Background Color on, the hero fades into the artwork's colour and the rows below sit on it.
- Animated collection covers on iPhone and iPad.
- Keyboard control of the player on iPhone and iPad: arrows, space and Esc.
- Decoder and subtitle auto-sync settings on iPhone and iPad.

Improved
- iPad: the Home hero and rows run behind the sidebar, and the stream picker is a wider, taller sheet docked to the bottom.
- Collection folders open with portrait posters by default, as imported from Xperience, with three across on iPhone.
- Tapping or clicking outside a player menu closes it.
- Loading indicators are centred everywhere.
- Search answers sooner and remembers recent results.
- Starting a stream on iPhone or iPad uses one connection instead of two.
- Hero trailers and animated covers rest in Low Power Mode.
- Email fields no longer capitalise the first letter.

Fixed
- Signing out on one device no longer signs out your others.
- If a session ends on its own, Omnia now tells you and keeps your data on the device. It syncs again when you sign in.
- Keys and sign-ins added while signed out are added to your account when you sign in, and anything missing from a device is restored.
- Settings dropdowns stay beside their title instead of dropping below it.
- Long titles no longer shrink their poster.
- Discover rows say "Popular - Movies" and "Popular - Series" instead of two rows called "Popular".
- The metadata cache now works after you reopen the app.
- Trailers close when they end.

Security
- Add-on install links now ask before installing.
- Your sign-in stays on the device instead of moving through backups.
- Copied add-on links stay on the device and clear after two minutes on iPhone and iPad.
- Keys are no longer saved in the network cache or in logs.
- Sign Out also clears saved video frames and the failure log.
- Profile PIN lockouts survive quitting the app.

privacy.NSFaceIDUsageDescription: Omnia uses Face ID to unlock Settings and profile switching when you turn those locks on.
privacy.NSLocalNetworkUsageDescription: Omnia connects to Jellyfin or Emby servers on your local network.
